extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of journalism history; general readers interested in press development
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter excerpt recounting the role, development, and social functions of American newspapers and journalists during and immediately after the Revolutionary War. Emphasizes institutional, technological, economic, and rhetorical aspects that shaped early American journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of the Press as a Canonical Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The liberty of the press is one of the canonical principles of the new nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a foundational legal and political norm that underpins the new nation's institutions and justifies press activity and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press as the Instrument of the People
rubrics_metrics.description: It was now regarded as their instrument, to which they had every right and in which the setting forth of their views was not to be stopped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press should represent popular opinion and act as a vehicle for citizens' views rather than a solely elite institution; legitimacy derives from being the people's instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counteracting Falsehoods and Sustaining Morale
rubrics_metrics.description: The patriotic press not only had to deny what was untruthful in the Loyalist press, but had to write, in the face of undeniable misfortune, what would be encouraging and would keep the weaker element from getting still weaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial strategy during crises: combine factual rebuttal of hostile propaganda with morale-boosting coverage aimed at retaining public support—avoid purely despairing accounts when it would demoralize the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Participation in Government and Public Life
rubrics_metrics.description: With the protection and encouragement of the press...its history is now one of development, and of participation in the development of the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and newspapers are expected to engage actively in political debates and public organization (e.g., organizing meetings, reporting conventions) rather than remaining aloof observers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of Public Documents (Publishing Laws)
rubrics_metrics.description: He printed the public laws gratuitously... Washington directed that he be paid: 'This is a debt of honor, and must be discharged.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing official laws and public documents is framed as a civic duty of the press; doing so may be treated as public service deserving official support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of Content Types to Serve Diverse Audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Their news was either very general or very local; the advertisements were matters of particular importance to the people locally. The essays and contributed editorials were of interest to those of culture and to those who had ideas and theories as to the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful paper balances general and local news, advertising (as an economic base and local service), and essays/editorials for the more cultured readership—tailor sections to audience segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity of Issuance and Local Presence as Civic Markers
rubrics_metrics.description: The dignity and prosperity of a town were established by the fact that it supported a weekly journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining a regular publication schedule and local operations conveys civic legitimacy and indicates a town's engagement with public affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and Transmission Infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Post-Office would not carry the papers and the post-riders had to be bribed... It took six days for a letter to go from Boston to New York.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely news depends on reliable transmission systems; logistical constraints (post, riders, travel times) significantly limit news timeliness and geographic reach—planning must account for these limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological and Material Self-sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The war had furnished a great incentive to American manufacturing; types, presses, paper and ink were now manufactured in this country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic production of printing materials is essential infrastructure for a robust press; technological/material capacity enables sustained and independent newspaper production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic Viability Shapes Format (Advertisements → Daily)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pennsylvania Packet... appeared as a daily, evidently in response to a large increase in the advertisements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic forces—especially advertising revenue—drive decisions about frequency and format; increasing ad demand can justify moving from weekly to daily publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Leadership and 'Leading' the Press
rubrics_metrics.description: It actually represented the people, the 'rabble'... except when it was properly 'led,' it was not considered a power for good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are expected to provide leadership that channels popular sentiment constructively; strong editorial direction increases the perceived civic value of the press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Accuracy and On-the-Scene Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: I took the pulpit for my reporting desk... I proceeded with my reports, generally to the acceptance of the Convention. I succeeded well enough in this my first effort to give a tolerable fair report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate reporting of public proceedings (even without formal stenography) is a key journalistic standard; being present and providing fair accounts of events confers authority and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Value of Personalities and Vivid Incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: News, in the sense of personalities, could not be carried further than he carried it in depicting the scene when his sanctum was invaded by an irate citizen... This was a news development that was afterward to be emulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human-interest, personal conflicts, and vivid incidents have high news value and engage readers—editors may emphasize personalities to increase circulation and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-Service Role: Warnings and Practical Information
rubrics_metrics.description: The papers of the colonies warned their readers to beware of counterfeiters and to take no French guineas 'till they had examined carefully the hair on the King's head.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond politics, newspapers serve practical public-service functions (consumer warnings, safety information); such content reinforces the press's civic utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press as Moral and Cultural Educator (Encouraging Reforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: He was for republican equality and against privilege. He was the first to urge an extension of independence to the enslaved negro; the first to arraign monarchy, to denounce dueling... to call for justice for women and kindliness toward animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorials and essays can advocate social reforms and influence cultural norms; the press is positioned as an agent for progressive political and moral ideas.
